'''Sir Stephen Philip Jackson''' (born 17 July 1962) is a British biologist who is the [[Quick Professor of Biology|Frederick James Quick Professor of Biology]]. He is a senior group leader at the [[Cancer Research UK]] Cambridge Institute and associate group leader at the [[Gurdon Institute]], [[University of Cambridge]].

==Education==
Jackson was educated at the [[University of Leeds]], graduating with a Bachelor of Science degree in biochemistry in 1983.<ref>[http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U21676 ‘JACKSON, Prof. Stephen Philip’] ''Who's Who 2014, A & C Black, an imprint of Bloomsbury Publishing plc, 2014; online edn, Oxford University Press, 2013''</ref> He then carried out his [[PhD]] research working with [[Jean Beggs]] on yeast RNA splicing at [[Imperial College London]] and [[Edinburgh University]], earning his PhD in 1987.<ref name=thesis>{{cite web|url=http://catalogue.lib.ed.ac.uk/vwebv/search?searchType=7&searchId=688&maxResultsPerPage=50&recCount=50&recPointer=0&resultPointer=0&headingId=2199567 |title=Cloning and characterisation of the RNA8 gene of ''Saccharomyces cerevisiae'' |last=Jackson |first=Stephen Phillip |year=1987 |type=PhD thesis |publisher=University of Edinburgh}}</ref>

==Research==
Following his PhD, Jackson carried out postdoctoral research with [[Robert Tjian]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he developed an interest in the regulation of [[gene transcription|transcription]]. He returned to the UK in 1991 as a Junior Group Leader at the then Wellcome-CRC Institute, now the [[Gurdon Institute]].

<!-- 'best known for' is uncited, and the source given for the 'group identified' is a just a group photo. As it stands, promotional -->
<!-- Jackson is best known for his work on cellular responses to DNA damage. His group identified many key DNA-damage-response (DDR) proteins and established how they interact with damaged DNA and with one another in regulated ways.<ref>https://www.stevejacksonlab.org/ {{bare URL inline|date=April 2023}}</ref> -->
Jackson's work has provided key insights into cellular processes that respond to [[DNA damage]]; processes fundamental to life and whose defects cause various diseases particularly cancer.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Jackson | first1 = SP | title = The DNA-damage response in human biology and disease. | doi = 10.1038/nature08467 | journal = Nature | volume = 461 | issue = 7267 | pages = 1071–1078 | year = 2009 | pmid = 19847258| pmc =2906700 | bibcode = 2009Natur.461.1071J }}</ref> Through his discovery that the DNA-dependent protein kinase (DNA-PK) enzyme is activated by DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs),<ref>{{Cite journal | vauthors = Gottlieb TM, Jackson SP | title = The DNA-dependent protein kinase: requirement for DNA ends and association with Ku antigen. | doi = 10.1016/0092-8674(93)90057-W | journal = Cell | volume = 72 | issue = 1 | pages = 131–142 | year = 1993 | pmid = 8422676| s2cid = 205020792 }}</ref> Jackson's laboratory identified and characterised various components of the [[non-homologous end joining]] (NHEJ) system that repairs most DSBs in human cells. These studies also provided a paradigm for Jackson's later work on DNA-damage signalling by the [[ATM serine/threonine kinase]] and ATR ([[Ataxia telangiectasia and Rad3 related]]),<ref name=Blackford>{{Cite journal | vauthors = Blackford AN, Jackson SP | title = ATM, ATR, and DNA-PK: The Trinity at the Heart of the DNA Damage Response. | doi = 10.1016/j.molcel.2017.05.015 | journal = Molecular Cell | volume = 66 | issue = 6 | pages = 801–817 | year = 2017 | pmid = 28622525| doi-access = free }}</ref> and his studies on how these and additional DNA repair factors interact with and influence one another, often in ways regulated by post-translational modifications.<ref name=Polo>{{Cite journal | vauthors = Polo SE, Jackson SP | title = Dynamics of DNA damage response proteins at DNA breaks: a focus on protein modifications. | doi = 10.1101/gad.2021311 | journal = Genes & Development | volume = 25 | issue = 5 | pages = 409–433 | year = 2011 | pmid = 21363960| pmc = 3049283}}</ref> Jackson's work has also helped establish how DSB repair is controlled during the cell cycle, at telomeres in response to cell aging/senescence, and within chromatin.<ref name=Blackford /><ref name=Polo /><ref>{{Cite journal | vauthors = D'Adda di Fagagna F, Teo SW, Jackson SP | title = Functional links between telomeres and proteins of the DNA-damage response. | doi = 10.1101/gad.1214504 | journal = Genes & Development | volume = 18 | issue = 15 | pages = 1781–1799 | year = 2004 | pmid = 15289453 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

In 1997 Jackson founded KuDOS Pharmaceuticals with the aim of translating knowledge of [[DNA repair|DNA damage response]] pathways into new treatments for cancer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cancerresearchuk.org/funding-for-researchers/research-features/2020-09-24-parp-inhibitors-halting-cancer-by-halting-dna-repair|title=PARP inhibitors: Halting cancer by halting DNA repair|publisher=Cancer Research UK|date=24 September 2020}}</ref> KuDOS developed small-molecule inhibitors of several DNA damage response enzymes. The most advanced of these is the poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 ([[PARP1]]) inhibitor [[Olaparib]]/Lynparza™, which is now a registered medicine worldwide.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.astrazeneca.com/media-centre/press-releases/2014/lynparza-approved-us-fda-brca-mutated-ovarian-cancer-treatment-19122014.html# |title=LYNPARZA™ approved by the US Food and Drug administration |publisher=AstraZeneca |type=press release |date=19 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/lynparza |title=EPAR Medicine Overview |publisher=European Medicines Agency |date=9 January 2015}}</ref> KuDOS developed into a fully integrated drug-discovery and drug-development company and was acquired by [[AstraZeneca]] in 2005.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.astrazeneca.com/Media/Press-releases/Article/20051223--Acquisition-Of-KuDOS-Pharmaceuticals-Will-Enhance-Ast |title=Acquisition Of KuDOS Pharmaceuticals Will Enhance AstraZeneca's Ability To Generate Novel Cancer Treatments |publisher=AstraZeneca |type=press release |date=23 December 2005}}</ref>

In 2011 Jackson founded MISSION Therapeutics<ref name="mission">{{cite web|url=https://missiontherapeutics.com/about-mission/management/ |website =Mission Therapeutics |title=Management}}</ref><ref name="JacksonLabAbout">{{cite web|url=http://www2.gurdon.cam.ac.uk/~jacksonlab/steve_jackson.htm |title=Steve Jackson |website=Steve Jackson Laboratory|date=7 August 2024 }}</ref> a firm to develop  drugs to  improve the management of life-threatening diseases, particularly cancer. In 2017, he founded Adrestia Therapeutics Ltd <ref name="adrestia">{{cite web |url=https://adrestia.squarespace.com/ |website=Adrestia Therapeutics |title=Adrestia Therapeutics |access-date=10 June 2019 |archive-date=29 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929110346/https://adrestia.squarespace.com/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> and currently serves as Chief Scientific Officer.

=== Paper retractions ===

In 2018, Jackson's former postdoctoral scholar, [[Abderrahmane Kaidi]], then working at the [[University of Bristol]] was found guilty of research fraud.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=2018-09-13 |title=Bristol lecturer resigns over fabricated research |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-bristol-45511492 |access-date=2023-09-18}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Yong |first=Michael |date=2018-09-14 |title=Bristol Uni lecturer resigns after faking research |url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/news/bristol-news/bristol-university-lecturer-resigns-fake-2005686 |access-date=2023-09-18 |website=BristolLive}}</ref> Kaidi additionally confessed that he had made false data in two of his research papers published with Jackson.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Mayo |first=Nick |date=2019-04-12 |title=Articles pulled after data fabrication in Cambridge DNA lab |url=https://digital.timeshighereducation.com/THE180419-F1h4m2/html5/index.html# |access-date=2023-09-18 |website=Times Higher Education}}</ref> Bristol conveyed the matter to the University of Cambridge which took up an investigation.<ref name=":22">{{Cite web |last=Yong |first=Michael |date=2018-09-14 |title=Bristol Uni lecturer resigns after faking research |url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/news/bristol-news/bristol-university-lecturer-resigns-fake-2005686 |access-date=2023-09-18 |website=BristolLive |language=en}}</ref>

On 19 August 2018, Cambridge and Jackson informed ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' that the paper published in 2010<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kaidi |first1=Abderrahmane |last2=Weinert |first2=Brian T. |last3=Choudhary |first3=Chunaram |last4=Jackson |first4=Stephen P. |date=2010-09-10 |title=RETRACTED: Human SIRT6 promotes DNA end resection through CtIP deacetylation|journal=Science |volume=329 |issue=5997 |pages=1348–1353 |doi=10.1126/science.1192049 |issn=1095-9203 |pmc=3276839 |pmid=20829486|bibcode=2010Sci...329.1348K }}{{Retracted|doi=10.1126/science.aax4558|pmid=30975768|http://retractionwatch.com/2018/09/29/weekend-reads-lessons-from-the-downfall-of-brian-wansink-scientific-terrorism-redux-why-cochrane-booted-a-member/ ''Retraction Watch''|http://retractionwatch.com/2019/04/11/authors-have-papers-in-nature-and-science-retracted-on-the-same-day/ ''Retraction Watch''|intentional=yes}}</ref> was investigated for research misconduct. The journal issued an [[expression of concern]] over the article the next month.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Berg |first=Jeremy |date=2018-09-28 |title=Editorial expression of concern |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aav4528 |journal=Science |volume=361 |issue=6409 |pages=1322 |doi=10.1126/science.aav4528 |issn=1095-9203 |pmid=30262489|bibcode=2018Sci...361.1322B |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Cambridge made its final decision in April 2019 that the paper in ''Science'' and another in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' (in 2013<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kaidi |first1=Abderrahmane |last2=Jackson |first2=Stephen P. |date=2013-06-06 |title=KAT5 tyrosine phosphorylation couples chromatin sensing to ATM signalling |journal=Nature |volume=498 |issue=7452 |pages=70–74 |doi=10.1038/nature12201 |pmc=3859897 |pmid=23708966|bibcode=2013Natur.498...70K }}{{Retracted|doi=10.1038/s41586-019-1142-2|pmid=30976101|http://retractionwatch.com/2019/04/11/authors-have-papers-in-nature-and-science-retracted-on-the-same-day/ ''Retraction Watch''|intentional=yes}}</ref>) contain fabricated data that were done by Kaidi.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Else |first=Holly |date=2019-04-15 |title=Top journals retract DNA-repair studies after misconduct probe |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-019-00406-4 |journal=Nature |doi=10.1038/d41586-019-00406-4|pmid=32284556 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Jackson was not involved in the misdeed.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-04-17 |title=Two Retractions |url=https://www.genomeweb.com/two-retractions |access-date=20 September 2023 |website=Genome Web}}</ref> The two journals simultaneously retracted the papers on 11 April 2019.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kaidi |first1=Abderrahmane |last2=Weinert |first2=Brian T. |last3=Choudhary |first3=Chunaram |last4=Jackson |first4=Stephen P. |date=2019-04-19 |title=Retraction [Human SIRT6 promotes DNA end resection through CtIP deacetylation] |journal=Science |volume=364 |issue=6437 |pages=247 |doi=10.1126/science.aax4558 |issn=1095-9203 |pmc=6558281 |pmid=30975768}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kaidi |first1=Abderrahmane |last2=Jackson |first2=Stephen P. |date=2019-04-11 |title=Retraction Note: KAT5 tyrosine phosphorylation couples chromatin sensing to ATM signalling |journal=Nature |volume=568 |issue=7753 |pages=576 |doi=10.1038/s41586-019-1142-2 |issn=1476-4687 |pmc=6554193 |pmid=30976101|bibcode=2019Natur.568..576K }}</ref>

In 2024 further evidence of scientific fraud was identified and another paper from Jackson's laboratory was retracted. This time the first author was Abdeladim Moumen, and the paper 'hnRNP K: An HDM2 Target and Transcriptional Coactivator of p53 in Response to DNA Damage' was retracted from Cell.  

==Honours and awards==
Jackson has received numerous awards, medals and honorary degrees: the inaugural Eppendorf-Nature European Young Investigator Award (1995);<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://corporate.eppendorf.com/en/company/scientific-awards/european-award/|title=European Award - Eppendorf Corporate|website=corporate.eppendorf.com}}</ref> the Tenovus Medal for Cancer Research (1997);<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gla.ac.uk/colleges/mvls/tenovus/previousmedalwinners/|title=University of Glasgow - Colleges - College of Medical, Veterinary & Life Sciences - Tenovus - Previous Medal Winners|access-date=25 September 2019|archive-date=7 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807153733/https://www.gla.ac.uk/colleges/mvls/tenovus/previousmedalwinners/|url-status=dead}}</ref> the [[Colworth Medal]] (1997); the Anthony Dipple Carcinogenesis Young Investigator award (2002);<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jackson |first1=S. P. |year=2002 |title=Sensing and repairing DNA double-strand breaks |url=https://academic.oup.com/carcin/article/23/5/687/2608214 |journal=Carcinogenesis |volume=23 |issue=5 |pages=687–696 |doi=10.1093/carcin/23.5.687 |pmid=12016139 |doi-access=free|url-access=subscription }}</ref> the [[Biochemical Society]] GlaxoSmithKline Award (2008);<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.biochemsoctrans.org/bst/037/bst0370483.htm|title=Biochemical Society Transactions &#124; Portland Press}}</ref> the [[BBSRC]] Innovator of the Year Award (2009);<ref>[http://www.bbsrc.ac.uk/business/fostering-innovation/innovator.aspx Innovator of the Year]</ref> the Royal Society Buchanan Medal (2011),<ref name=medal>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/grants-schemes-awards/awards/buchanan-medal/|title=Buchanan Medal &#124; Royal Society|website=royalsociety.org|date=29 November 2024 }}</ref> the latter in recognition of his "outstanding contributions to understanding DNA repair and DNA damage response signalling pathways", and the Gagna A. & Ch. Van Heck Prize (2015) for "his cardinal contributions related to cellular events that detect, signal the presence of and repair DNA damages".<ref name="University of Cambridge Awards">{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Glynn |date=18 November 2015 |title=Gagna A. & Ch. Van Heck Prize awarded to Professor Steve Jackson |url=https://www.staff.admin.cam.ac.uk/awards/gagna-a-ch-van-heck-prize-awarded-to-professor-steve-jackson |website=For staff}}</ref> 

Jackson is the co-winner of the [[King Faisal International Prize]] for Science 2016, in recognition of his "outstanding contribution to defining the link between the basic mechanism of genomic DNA instability and its relationship to cancer. Specifically, he unraveled the salient components of the pathway involved in DNA repair. He is also credited with an innovative approach to bring his findings into tangible therapeutic products to treat cancer".<ref name="Gurdon Institute News 20.01.16">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gurdon.cam.ac.uk/news/jackson-2016-faisal-prize|title=20.01.16 Steve Jackson wins 2016 King Faisal International Prize|date=20 January 2016|website=www.gurdon.cam.ac.uk|access-date=1 May 2021|archive-date=29 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211129093047/https://www.gurdon.cam.ac.uk/news/jackson-2016-faisal-prize|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was elected a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO) in 1997, a Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences in 2001<ref name=fmedsci>{{Cite web|url=http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/professor-stephen-jackson/|title=The Academy of Medical Sciences &#124; Directory of Fellows|access-date=23 June 2014|archive-date=14 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220314171718/https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/professor-stephen-jackson/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and a Fellow of the Royal Society in 2008.<ref name=frs>{{cite web |url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Persons&dsqPos=0&dsqSearch=%28%28text%29%3D%27Jackson,%20Stephen%27%29 |title=Jackson; Stephen Philip |publisher=The Royal Society |accessdate=24 August 2014 |archive-date=29 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220329154601/https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Persons&dsqPos=0&dsqSearch=%28%28text%29%3D%27Jackson,%20Stephen%27%29 |url-status=dead }}</ref> 

In 2016, Jackson was awarded the [[Heineken Prizes|Dr A. H. Heineken Prize for Medicine]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/awards/heineken-prizes/stephen-jackson |title=Heineken Prizes - Stephen Jackson |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |accessdate=10 May 2016 |archive-date=16 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016074932/https://www.knaw.nl/en/awards/heineken-prizes/stephen-jackson |url-status=dead }}</ref> for his "fundamental research into DNA repair in human cells and for the successful application of knowledge of that process in the development of new cancer drugs".<ref name="Gurdon Institute News 10.05.16">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gurdon.cam.ac.uk/news/heineken-prize|title=10.05.16 Steve Jackson wins the 2016 Dr A.H. Heineken Prize for Medicine|date=9 May 2016|website=www.gurdon.cam.ac.uk|access-date=1 May 2021|archive-date=26 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726134000/https://www.gurdon.cam.ac.uk/news/heineken-prize|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2017 he was awarded the Genome Stability Network medal for his contributions to the field of genome stability and particularly for the realisation of the therapeutic potential of targeting the DDR.<ref name="GSN News and Events">{{Cite web|url=http://www.genomestabilitynetwork.org.uk/UK_GSN/News_and_Events.html|title=News & Events|website=www.genomestabilitynetwork.org.uk|access-date=22 June 2017|archive-date=20 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420072144/http://genomestabilitynetwork.org.uk/UK_GSN/News_and_Events.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

The Fondation ARC's Leopold Griffuel Prize in Translational and Clinical Research was presented to Jackson in 2019 for his work on DNA damage repair and his role in the development of medicines such as PARP1 and 2 inhibitors, currently used for cancer treatment.<ref name="Gurdon Institute News 11.04.19">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gurdon.cam.ac.uk/news/leopold-griffuel-jackson|title=11.02.19 Steve Jackson to receive the ARC Foundation's Léopold Griffuel Award|date=11 February 2019|website=www.gurdon.cam.ac.uk|access-date=6 June 2019|archive-date=14 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414075203/https://www.gurdon.cam.ac.uk/news/leopold-griffuel-jackson|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="47e Prix Fondation ARC Léopold Griffuel  10.04.19">{{Cite web|url=https://www.fondation-arc.org/actualites/2019/47e-prix-fondation-arc-leopold-griffuel|title=47e Prix Fondation ARC Léopold Griffuel &#124; Fondation ARC pour la recherche sur le cancer|website=www.fondation-arc.org}}</ref> In 2020, he was awarded the Royal Society's [[Mullard Award]] for his research on DNA repair mechanisms and synthetic lethality that led to the discovery of olaparib which has reached blockbuster status for the treatment of ovarian and breast cancers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stevejacksonlab.org/edit-news/2020/8/4/steve-jackson-2020-recipient-of-the-royal-society-mullard-award|title=Steve Jackson 2020 recipient of the Royal Society Mullard Award|date=4 August 2020|website=Steve Jackson Laboratory}}</ref> 

In 2022, Jackson was awarded the Johann Anton Merck Award, which is given for outstanding scientific preclinical research accomplishments in the areas of Merck Healthcare‘s strategic focus.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.merckgroup.com/en/research/grants-and-awards/johann-anton-merck-award.html|title=2022 Johann Anton Merck Award|date=14 July 2022|website=Merck Group|access-date=16 March 2023|archive-date=4 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220804164820/https://www.merckgroup.com/en/research/grants-and-awards/johann-anton-merck-award.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Cancer Research UK]] honoured Steve with Cancer Research Horizon's Entrepreneurship Recognition Award in recognition of his longstanding academic entrepreneurship and his outstanding contributions that have enhanced the field of oncology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cancerresearchhorizons.com/innovation-entrepreneurship-awards-2022|title=Innovation and Entrepreneurship Awards 2022|date=9 December 2022|website=Cancer Research Horizons}}</ref>

Jackson was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in the [[2023 Birthday Honours]] for services to innovation and research.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=64082|supp=y|page=B2|date=17 June 2023}}</ref>
